Does anybody have much experience in creating their own mixes, for example, a seed germination mix or transplanting mix?

What have you found useful?

If you're doing it indoors, you want it to be sterile. I don't have much experience here, but I've heard coconut fibre is a good alternative to starting soil as it holds water like peat moss.

I personally use seed starting mix as I know it's sterile and cheap.

I generally stick with a good quality potting soil for a base, and incorporate peat, vermiculite, sands, and perlite to obtain the texture, pH, and water retention I want. Once I start to pot things up as they outgrow 1/2 inch seed flats, I usually start incorporating soil from under my compost pile to build a microorganism population.

I think for general garden vegetables, you are typically fine with a bagged seed starting medium, and potting up with regular bagged potting soil. If you have the space it's a fun experiment to try various mixes and see results. The biggest issue you will run into is damping off, so ensure you do not have standing water in the bottom of the flat, and plenty of air circulation.

As I pot up, I will fill the containers with layers of different medium mixes to encourage root development downward. For a more complex example calluna (heather) will be started in a 1/2 inch flat fill halfway with vermiculite and peat in equal proportions, topped with bagged seed starting mix and peat that has been pretty heavily burned, topped with a good dusting of pine needle ash. When I pot them up, the bottom of the container is equal parts peat and soil from under the compost, packed in around the sides with equal parts potting soil, peat, and vermiculite. This allows good drainage on top, forcing the roots to develop downwards to reach moisture. If the leaves start to get too dark I will water with a mix of sterilized balsamic vinegar and water.
